1.rule: with a device, the device keeps the log's head and signs a fresh read of it on request: a forged log fails verification and the next launch refuses it
1.reason: host already compromised: a same-user process can rewrite the log and its head together

2.rule: the launch is refused unless the person approved the measured code and policy with the device; with a device, every call's decision is also committed to the device, and verification re-decides every call from the committed policy
2.reason: host already compromised: a same-user process can replace the code before it starts

3.rule: every device answer is checked against the genuine device's certified identity

4.rule: every device answer is signed over a fresh nonce of the caller's; a replayed answer is refused

5.rule: an uncertified or cloned device is refused

6.rule: with a device, Claude Code's login is sealed under the device and held only in memory during a session; detaching the device halts the session and kills every process it started

7.rule: activation needs a FIDO2 key or a device-bound passkey, and with a device a code the device verifies itself; a device unlock is bound to its ticket and the credential that signed it
7.reason: host already compromised: a same-user process can replace the enrolled key, or run plain \texttt{claude}

1d.rule: an anchor session opens only with an activation the person produced on the device, and every record it anchors names that activation; verification refuses a head that names none of the log's own launches

2-smart.rule: the device signs each call's decision; the launcher stops the session when the hook reports another, and verification re-decides every call from the committed policy

7-outside-job.rule: a device unlock is bound to one job (the approved code, the policy, the project and the kind of session); the device refuses a launch outside it

8-poison.rule: a file changed outside the agent is blocked for reading, running and loading; a person may allow a changed file only if it is not executable, and every detection, block and approval is audited

gate/F1.rule: options parsed as \texttt{getopt} does, against each command's specification

gate/F2.rule: checks run on the resolved path; a write through a symbolic link asks

gate/F3.rule: names compared after NFC normalization and case folding

gate/F4.rule: a scratch directory that overlaps the project is ignored

gate/F5.rule: an unlisted host asks; denied with an enforced allowlist

gate/F6.rule: a git read asks when the repository's git configuration can start a program

gate/R1.rule: any prefix of a refused long option, or of its \texttt{no-} form, is refused

gate/R2.rule: targets compared by device and inode with protected files: denied

gate/R3.rule: a target with more than one hard link asks

gate/C1.rule: linear-time cleaner under time budgets; past a budget the content is withheld

gate/C2.rule: Select Graphic Rendition parameters parsed left to right

gate/D1.rule: code-point scan to a fixed point; lone surrogates stripped

gate/D2.rule: control characters rendered as a terminal shows them

gate/D3.rule: notices arrive only out of band; imitations neutralized

gate/D5.rule: decisions bound by resolved absolute paths with a real path-boundary check

gate/E2.rule: agent-controlled values quoted, capped and labeled untrusted; the real path shown

gate/E1.rule: notices out of band; imitations matched on a normalized skeleton

gate/E3.rule: nesting resolved in one pass; only the offending region is withheld

gate/E4.rule: single joiners kept where they carry meaning

gate/E5.rule: notices out of band, and each says what it covers

integrity/I1.rule: the hook takes no configuration from its environment: digest-pinned session file, \texttt{env -i}

integrity/I1b.rule: the hook starts under \texttt{env -i} with absolute paths

integrity/I1c.rule: the hardware mode comes from the session file; only a root-owned administrator file can relax it

integrity/I2.rule: user settings validated against Claude Code's own schema; the launch handshake is required

integrity/I3.rule: \cz{}'s own files are protected paths: writes denied

integrity/I4.rule: a project that contains the install or the state refuses the launch

integrity/I5.rule: a gap record is written before the next append; verification fails

integrity/I6.rule: a head anchor without a log fails verification

integrity/I7.rule: the device keeps the log's head
integrity/I7.reason: host already compromised: a same-user process can write the log and its head together

integrity/I8.rule: every answer checked against the genuine device

integrity/I9a.rule: repository hooks refuse the launch; an input changed after the decision is detected

integrity/I10.rule: managed hooks recognized only when structurally equal to the template

integrity/I11.rule: every command that starts a session gets the hooks

integrity/I12.rule: restore entries come only from audit records

integrity/I13.rule: restore by audit entry identifier, to the recorded path only

integrity/I14.rule: the session directory is private (0700) and outside the project

integrity/R1.rule: a lock that is not a regular file fails closed at once

integrity/N1.rule: nested schema validation; every \texttt{PreToolUse} held until the handshake

integrity/N2.rule: peer-checked control socket and a challenge chained into the audit log

integrity/N3.rule: hooks recognized exactly, from every source; any other refuses the launch

integrity/N4.rule: a headless run is treated as headless however its output is connected

integrity/N5.rule: secret paths denied to every read tool and shell command

integrity/N6.rule: a background session is refused while a hardware root is in use

integrity/N7.rule: every process the session started is killed before the erase

integrity/N9.rule: schema validation; any repository hook refuses the launch; each decision bound to the call in the transcript

integrity/N10.rule: heads are anchored only by the launcher, extending the chain it verified
integrity/N10.reason: host already compromised: without a device, a same-user process can write the log and its head together

integrity/N10b.rule: an older anchor fails verification; the anchor history is kept

integrity/N12.rule: child subreaper, transient scope and session marker: every process the session started is killed

integrity/N7b.rule: every process the session started is killed before the erase; a watcher re-erases

integrity/F1.rule: generated validator; a headless run stops on Claude Code's ``did not load'' message

integrity/F2.rule: a command-valued project setting refuses the launch unless an administrator granted it

integrity/N13.rule: each decision is reported; a call that ran against its decision stops the session

integrity/N14.rule: the launcher anchors only heads that extend the chain it followed; tampering stops the session
integrity/N14.reason: host already compromised: without a device, a same-user process can write the log and its head together

integrity/N15.rule: the launch stops with an alarm; no call runs unchecked

integrity/R5-A.rule: launch-time check against the device's head; refused until a person accepts with two factors
integrity/R5-A.reason: host already compromised: without a device, a same-user process can replace the log and its head between sessions

integrity/N13c.rule: an approval counts only when typed at \cz{}'s own prompt

integrity/R5-L.rule: refused while an operator private key is on the host; operators sign offline
